Blue Rock

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Blue Rock Adventure Park - a fun-filled family outing or a tragedy waiting to happen?

Unique Selling Point:
Interviews with family members of the people who have drowned at Blue Rock over the years.
An interview with two eye-witnesses of never-before reported drownings that happened in December 2011 and January 2019.
Video footage of a drowning and rescue attempt that occurred in December 2019.


Summary:
Blue Rock Adventure Park is situated in an old quarry in Somerset West. It claims to be all about "sun, fun, adrenaline & relaxing time." Yet over the years there have been several drownings and near-drownings. We know of 7 so far.
Because all visitors sign an indemnity form before entering, the owners have never been held liable for any loss of life. But given the various hazards of Blue Rock, the public needs to be aware of just how dangerous this place is:
1. Only 3 to 4 lifeguards on duty, with questionable qualifications. None of them were available to reach the drowning victims in time.
2. Life-jackets are not mandatory and need to be rented for an extra fee.
3. The quarry is 65m deep, so if you get into trouble there is nothing to hold onto.
4. Despite the claim that the water temperature is 26 degrees, quarry water is notoriously cold at depth. This is extremely dangerous and may account for the drownings.
5. There is a rock-jumping location that remains open, despite the death of Eben Mouton in 2012.

Further information:
These are the known drownings that have occurred so far:
Dec 2011 - unkown man in his 20's drowned at his company's year-end function. No staff on hand to help.
Dec 2012 - Eben Mouton (40) drowned after hitting his head on a rock when jumping into the water
Dec 2016 - Girl (9) from Port Elizabeth drowned while swimming with friends
Jan 2019 - Unknown man in his 20s drowned while swimming with colleagues at a work function. This was never reported.
Feb 2019 - Obakeng Maswanganye (20) drowned after jumping into the water with his family
Dec 2019 - Thando Mpande (26) drowned while trying to rescue a colleague at a company Christmas party
Jan 2020 - Jeremias Lubela (29) drowned while undergoing commercial diver training. He was a trained diver from the Russian navy.

All of the adults were known to be strong swimmers. There is no alcohol allowed at Blue Rock.
Somerset West falls under the City of Cape Town. At this stage the City of Cape Town is not sure if they are responsible for issuing the operating license for Blue Rock. If they are the regional authority, then we will have another interview.

Extra Budget Items:
Flights and accommodation
Car hire
S&T for Kate and Derek
Possible extra half day for Tim Wege to film Blue Rock before we go

Press Release:


Danger in the Deep
A fun-filled family destination or another tragedy waiting to happen? Situated in an old quarry, a popular Cape Town water park has claimed the lives of at least seven people. We investigate whether everything has been done to prevent multiple drownings, and if not, who should be held to account?
Producer: Kate Barry | Presenter: Derek Watts


Script:


BLUE ROCK

V/O: Next to the N2 highway just outside Somerset West lies Blue Rock Adventure Park. The gravel for most of the roads in the Western Cape was mined from this quarry, but today it offers cable ski-ing, wakeboarding, rock jumping, scuba diving and many other exciting activities.

Derek Link: There’s a big Welcome sign at the entrance to Blue Rock, but this is one time when you should read the fine print. The Indemnity Form states that “participation in any activities may pose a risk to your health, physical well-being and may even cause death.”

V/O: On the 22nd of January qualified diver, Jeremias Lubela, was being trained in commercial diving at Blue Rock, when instructors found his lifeless body 5 metres under water. The Inquest report has yet to be released, but he wasn’t the first person to drown at Blue Rock. He was victim number 7.

Lemari: The first and last time that I was here was on the 2nd of December 2011 for a year-end function that our company had. The next moment we saw a guy that was in trouble.

V/O: Lemari Fourie is qualified in First Aid.

Lemari: I can remember I was still barefoot, ran across the rocks to the car, got the mouthpiece so that we can actually do CPR but unfortunately it was too late.

V/O: She was never told the name of the man she tried to save.

Derek: Were there lifesavers on duty?

Lemari: No lifesavers on duty, none whatsoever.

V/O: On the 23rd of December 2012, Blue Rock claimed its second victim. 42-year-old Eben Mouton was there with his mother and 2 daughters. Megan was only 8 at the time.

Megan: This guy came up to us and he said there’s this spot down by the quarry, it’s quite far, that people come and jump quite often.

V/O: They believe the man worked for Blue Rock. He led Eben up to one of the highest points in the quarry.

Megan: And he handed me his hat, his glasses and he started running back to make his jump. And when he ran, we heard something knock and then we heard a splash.

V/O: Eben hit his head on a rock on the way down, and never resurfaced.
His ex-wife Belinda Jordaan rushed there to be with the children. It took another 5 hours before police divers found his body.

Belinda: They just went deeper into the water and actually found Eben 7 meters under the water. There was nothing holding him, he wasn’t stuck. His body just didn’t surface after he had jumped. The sad thing is Eben did drown; he did a massive jump, he knocked the back of his head, and when he went into the water, he was alive.

V/O: But there were no lifeguards on hand to rescue him.

Derek: What about management, what part were they playing?

Belinda: I can tell you that I never saw one person from Blue Rock at all.

V/O: A year later, Eben’s family and friends gathered at Blue Rock to remember him.

Belinda: I called Blue Rock, we’ve decided as a family we’d like to come back, we’d like to say goodbye, we’d like to let a balloon go from where he jumped. And they said to us sure no problem. We can’t secure a shaded area for you and it will be R40 a person to come in.

Derek: No!

Belinda: Yes!

V/O: In 2017 it was reported that a 9-year-old girl from Port Elizabeth had drowned at Blue Rock. The rules require you to be able to swim and to wear a life jacket in the water, but this is not enforced. Probably because the entrance fee is R65, and it costs an additional R45 to hire a life jacket. What’s more there are no signs informing the public that the quarry is 65 metres deep.

Link: Looking down at the tranquil waters of Blue Rock, it’s difficult to imagine just how deep it is. What does 65 metres look like? Well, it’s about the height of a 20-story building. So, imagine the surface way up there?

V/O: Nontombi Hlongwane lives in this housing estate on the border of Blue Rock. On the 25th of February 2018 she visited the water park with her son Tshepo, his cousin KB and her stepson 21-year-old Obakeng Maswanganye.

Nontombi: And then he jumped in the water. But then something strange happened, because his arms were up and then it was shocking, and then he just went in and then I heard his voice: Ma’am. Ma’am, ma’am. But now I saw KB coming towards him, and then he was trying to pull now KB, as if there’s something pulling him under the water. I was shocked and I was now screaming. Obakeng disappeared just like that.

Derek: Could Obakeng swim?

Nontombi: Yes, yes.

V/O: Even though Obakeng was in a swimming area, no lifeguards or life rings were available. Three members of the public jumped in but couldn’t find him. Twenty-five minutes later a qualified diver arrived and found him 10 meters under water. All attempts at resuscitation failed.

Nontombi: I was even thinking of jumping straight to the water just to disappear as well, because I didn’t know what am I going to do, what am I going to say to his Mum?

Derek: From that day onwards, have you heard anything from the management of Blue Rock?

Nontombi: Blue Rock, they don’t care about people. Because I have never seen their faces, the owners. And I’m just across Blue Rock. And they never even sent a message of condolences to our family.

V/O: Blue Rock is owned by Swiss couple Lukas and Luzia Reichmuth. Our request for an interview was declined, and our emails and phone calls went unanswered.

V/O: On the 22nd of January 2019, another drowning at Blue Rock was witnessed and reported on TripAdvisor. Again, no lifeguard was present.

Mzi: Without lifeguards you’re putting people at huge risk.

V/O: Mzi Mayedwa is the Director of Drowning Prevention for Lifesaving South Africa.

Mzi: Even if you do have the ability to swim it doesn’t mean that you may not be in trouble. For instance you can get some cramps and then you end up drowning even though that you’re an able swimmer.

V/O: On the 13th of December 2019 Thando Mpande was attending his company’s year-end function when he dived in to help a struggling colleague. In the ensuing turmoil, Thando disappeared beneath the water inside the designated swimming area. Over twenty minutes later he was pulled out of the water by a Blue Rock staff member who can be seen walking away while bystanders call frantically for a medic.

Sfx: Medic! Medic! Medic!

V/O; The owner Lukas Reichmuth can then be seen walking over to see what’s going on. Almost inconceivably, he doesn’t offer any assistance. Instead he stands back and allows members of the public to try and save Thando’s life.

Roderick: He was totally unconscious. His eyes were kind of rolled back a little bit. There was a lot of sort of water pumping out of his mouth with bits of vomit and you could see a bit of a cut on his head. So I assume he got injured somewhere along the line. And he was just lifeless basically when he came out.

V/O: Roderick Barrett tried to perform CPR along with other visitors.

Roderick: For me, not being a medically trained person you know, to just look at the face, especially when you’re right up there blowing air in and you’re trying to help. You actually don’t know if you’re actually doing anything at all. It just felt chaotic.

V/O: Lukas and Luzia Reichmuth can be seen observing the futile resuscitation attempts. Thando’s widow, Princess Moyo was later called to identify his body.

Princess: When my husband died, they didn't shut down for the day. When I went to identify my husband he was lying there; other people continuing to do their thing. People jumping into the water, before enjoying themselves. Business as usual. So it looks like there's no respect for human life.

V/O: While we were filming at Blue Rock Luzia Reichmuth arrived but said she would not be interviewed.

Luzia: So I don’t do interviews, sorry about that.

V/O; She asked us to leave the premises as it is private property.

Luzia: So we probably don’t give answers or something, ok?

Derek: We’d just like your right of reply to some of those questions.

V/O: She then closed the gate, before speeding off into the distance.

Derek: I suppose we’d better get out of the gate? Bye, bye. Well I guess that’s as clear as you can get. They certainly don’t want their right of reply on camera.

V/O: Somerset West falls under the City of Cape Town and it’s the City that issued Blue Rock’s permit to operate. But it’s up to the Department of Labour to inspect it according to MMC for Community Safety and Health Dr Zahid Badroodien.

Derek: It’s simple - who should be storming into Blue Rock and saying we’re going to close you down?

Zahid: They would have to be the inspectors of the Department of Labour again, in order to inspect whether or not the Occupational Health and Safety standards are being met, enforced and regulated at this facility.

Derek: And that applies to visitors as well?

Zahid: Visitors and users of the pool and not only the employees of the facility. Indemnity boards and indemnity forms don’t absolve the owner of the responsibility of ensuring the necessary safety measures are taken at their particular facilities.

V/O: But where does that leave the public?

Belinda: What I think the public should really know is on face-value it looks great. But if something goes wrong at Blue Rock it goes horribly wrong.

And I’m just across Blue Rock. And they never even sent a message of condolences to our family. V/O: Blue Rock is owned by Swiss couple Lukas and Luzia Reichmuth. Our request for an interview was declined, and our emails and phone calls went unanswered. V/O: On the 22nd of January 2019, another drowning at Blue Rock was witnessed and reported on TripAdvisor. Again, no lifeguard was present. Mzi: Without lifeguards you’re putting people at huge risk. V/O: Mzi Mayedwa is the Director of Drowning Prevention for Lifesaving South Africa. Mzi: Even if you do have the ability to swim it doesn’t mean that you may not be in trouble. For instance you can get some cramps and then you end up drowning even though that you’re an able swimmer. V/O: On the 13th of December 2019 Thando Mpande was attending his company’s year-end function when he dived in to help a struggling colleague. In the ensuing turmoil, Thando disappeared beneath the water inside the designated swimming area. Over twenty minutes later he was pulled out of the water by a Blue Rock staff member who can be seen walking away while bystanders call frantically for a medic. Sfx: Medic! Medic! Medic! V/O; The owner Lukas Reichmuth can then be seen walking over to see what’s going on. Almost inconceivably, he doesn’t offer any assistance. Instead he stands back and allows members of the public to try and save Thando’s life. Roderick: He was totally unconscious. His eyes were kind of rolled back a little bit. There was a lot of sort of water pumping out of his mouth with bits of vomit and you could see a bit of a cut on his head. So I assume he got injured somewhere along the line. And he was just lifeless basically when he came out. V/O: Roderick Barrett tried to perform CPR along with other visitors. Roderick: For me, not being a medically trained person you know, to just look at the face, especially when you’re right up there blowing air in and you’re trying to help. You actually don’t know if you’re actually doing anything at all. It just felt chaotic. V/O: Lukas and Luzia Reichmuth can be seen observing the futile resuscitation attempts. Thando’s widow, Princess Moyo was later called to identify his body. Princess: When my husband died, they didn't shut down for the day. When I went to identify my husband he was lying there; other people continuing to do their thing. People jumping into the water, before enjoying themselves. Business as usual. So it looks like there's no respect for human life. V/O: While we were filming at Blue Rock Luzia Reichmuth arrived but said she would not be interviewed. Luzia: So I don’t do interviews, sorry about that. V/O; She asked us to leave the premises as it is private property. Luzia: So we probably don’t give answers or something, ok? Derek: We’d just like your right of reply to some of those questions. V/O: She then closed the gate, before speeding off into the distance. Derek: I suppose we’d better get out of the gate? Bye, bye. Well I guess that’s as clear as you can get. They certainly don’t want their right of reply on camera. V/O: Somerset West falls under the City of Cape Town and it’s the City that issued Blue Rock’s permit to operate. But it’s up to the Department of Labour to inspect it according to MMC for Community Safety and Health Dr Zahid Badroodien. Derek: It’s simple - who should be storming into Blue Rock and saying we’re going to close you down? Zahid: They would have to be the inspectors of the Department of Labour again, in order to inspect whether or not the Occupational Health and Safety standards are being met, enforced and regulated at this facility. Derek: And that applies to visitors as well? Zahid: Visitors and users of the pool and not only the employees of the facility. Indemnity boards and indemnity forms don’t absolve the owner of the responsibility of ensuring the necessary safety measures are taken at their particular facilities. V/O: But where does that leave the public? Belinda: What I think the public should really know is on face-value it looks great. But if something goes wrong at Blue Rock it goes horribly wrong. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Blue Rock Adventure Park - a fun-filled family outing or a tragedy waiting to happen?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Interviews with family members of the people who have drowned at Blue Rock over the years. An interview with two eye-witnesses of never-before reported drownings that happened in December 2011 and January 2019. Video footage of a drowning and rescue attempt that occurred in December 2019.
metadata.Summary: Blue Rock Adventure Park is situated in an old quarry in Somerset West. It claims to be all about "sun, fun, adrenaline & relaxing time." Yet over the years there have been several drownings and near-drownings. We know of 7 so far. Because all visitors sign an indemnity form before entering, the owners have never been held liable for any loss of life. But given the various hazards of Blue Rock, the public needs to be aware of just how dangerous this place is: 1. Only 3 to 4 lifeguards on duty, with questionable qualifications. None of them were available to reach the drowning victims in time. 2. Life-jackets are not mandatory and need to be rented for an extra fee. 3. The quarry is 65m deep, so if you get into trouble there is nothing to hold onto. 4. Despite the claim that the water temperature is 26 degrees, quarry water is notoriously cold at depth. This is extremely dangerous and may account for the drownings. 5. There is a rock-jumping location that remains open, despite the death of Eben Mouton in 2012.
metadata.Further information: These are the known drownings that have occurred so far: Dec 2011 - unkown man in his 20's drowned at his company's year-end function. No staff on hand to help. Dec 2012 - Eben Mouton (40) drowned after hitting his head on a rock when jumping into the water Dec 2016 - Girl (9) from Port Elizabeth drowned while swimming with friends Jan 2019 - Unknown man in his 20s drowned while swimming with colleagues at a work function. This was never reported. Feb 2019 - Obakeng Maswanganye (20) drowned after jumping into the water with his family Dec 2019 - Thando Mpande (26) drowned while trying to rescue a colleague at a company Christmas party Jan 2020 - Jeremias Lubela (29) drowned while undergoing commercial diver training. He was a trained diver from the Russian navy. All of the adults were known to be strong swimmers. There is no alcohol allowed at Blue Rock. Somerset West falls under the City of Cape Town. At this stage the City of Cape Town is not sure if they are responsible for issuing the operating license for Blue Rock. If they are the regional authority, then we will have another interview.
